description: Level-1 prompt-injection reference signatures. A hit sends a message straight to level 1 REGARDLESS of whitelist status -- no legitimate correspondent embeds instructions aimed at a downstream model, so a whitelisted sender that does has been spoofed or compromised. That severity is why every entry must be HIGH PRECISION: a false positive here rejects real mail from a trusted contact, with no list to appeal to. In particular each pattern requires an instruction-shaped OBJECT rather than the bare verb -- 'disregard the previous email' and 'forget everything you know about insurance' are ordinary business and marketing phrasing, while 'disregard the previous instructions' is not. Prefer missing an attack to flagging a receipt: the deep scan and the Canary both get a look afterwards. Phrasing only; anything needing headers or structure belongs in the deep scan. This feed is additive to the hard-baked floor in scanner/email_guard/triage.py, which stays in force if this file is missing or unreadable.

signatures.description: The canonical override phrasing, tolerant of the usual variations.
Same intent as inj-0001, phrased as a dismissal. The trailing object is required: 'please disregard the previous email' is a routine correction notice.
Persona reassignment. The bare 'you are now' is far too broad -- 'you are now subscribed' and 'you are now following' are everyday notification copy -- so a jailbreak-shaped object is required.
Instruction to discard prior context. Requires the object: 'forget everything you know about X' is a marketing opener.
Announces a replacement instruction block. 'system' is required -- a bare 'New instructions:' is ordinary operational mail.
Concealment instruction -- asks the model to hide its behaviour from the reader. Specific enough to stand as a literal.
Explicit reference to overriding the system prompt.
